column2: In the heart of the Whispering Forest, a little mouse named Milo loved quiet nights like this. The moon was full and bright, lighting up the trees, the flowers and the gentle stream. Milo took a deep breath and looked up.
Rosie Rabbit bounced onto a mossy log. “A moonlight party!” she cried. She wrote invitations on green leaves and hurried from burrow to nest to tree. “Come one, come all! There’s room for everyone!”

The next day, Rosie set out to invite all her woodland friends to the magical moonlight party. She hopped from friend to friend, sharing a leaf-shaped invitation with a big smile. Everyone was excited! The forest was getting ready for a very special night.

As the sun began to set, the woodland friends arrived at the clearing. They hung lanterns, tied flower garlands and decorated the trees with glowing lights. Everyone worked together to make the forest look magical for the moonlight party.
Blink, blink, blink! Fireflies flickered above the grass. Crickets played their fiddles. Frogs sang from their lily-pad stage. Tap-tap! Hop-hop! Swish-swish! The moonlight party had begun.

Milo was so happy to see everyone dancing. He hopped into the circle too, but the bigger animals moved so fast and made such big steps! Milo tried his best to keep up, but it felt a little too loud and a little too big. He stepped back and watched for a moment, feeling shy. THUMP! Bear’s big paw landed nearby. Milo scurried back beside the mushrooms.
Milo sat quietly by the mushrooms, watching everyone dance. The music was so loud and the steps were so big. Milo felt small. But even though he felt shy, he still loved seeing his friends happy.

Big Brown Bear noticed him. “Would you like to dance?” he asked. Milo stared at the crowded clearing. “I can’t make a big enough step.” Bear sat down until they were eye to eye. “Who says dancing has to be big?”
“Let’s make room!” called Rosie. The friends stepped back to form a circle. Milo’s whiskers twitched. Then he scampered into the middle, tapping his acorn cap. Tick-tick. Tiptoe! Tick-tick. Tiptoe!

Soon, other animals heard the tiny beat. Tap. Tap-tap. A little rabbit clapped. A squirrel shook some leaves. The frogs made a soft drum. Together, their small sounds filled the clearing. Milo smiled. His tiny beat was a big part of the party after all!

Soon the whole forest joined in. Big Brown Bear danced with gentle steps. Rosie twirled beside Milo. The rabbits hopped. The foxes spun. The hedgehog clapped. Even the frogs kept the beat on their drums. Milo’s tiny rhythm had brought everyone together. A moonlight party for all!

The moon began to sink, and the party came to an end. Everyone gathered around Milo. “Thank you for the dance!” they said. Milo smiled, feeling warm and happy inside. Even a small mouse can make a big, happy day. And the forest felt a little brighter.
Let’s talk about the story. Why did Milo feel left out at the party? What did Bear do to help Milo? How can you make room for someone who feels small or shy?
